threads.title: Pooled QCs, blanks and other instrument checks sit among the samples as if they were participants
threads.detector: reference_rows.pooled_qc_finding, name-blind: a minority level of a 2-10-level column whose rows vary far less across the feature block and carry no covariates. On metabolomics_untargeted that level is sample_type = pooled_qc (8 of 80 rows): median RSD 0.25 against 0.59 in participants, and no age, sex, BMI or responder. Two additions keep the test from missing references that are not simply tight: a dilution-series QC varies by design, so it is found by proportionality to the pool (its log profile is the pool's plus one constant offset across features); a long-term reference or NIST SRM 1950 is as tight as the pool, so it is told apart from the pool by its distance from the study centroid. The sample_roles naming census adds blanks, calibrants, dilution series, LTRs and system-suitability injections, as a guess only. Alternatives it must reject: a small real subgroup (varies like everyone else and has covariates); a name-only guess (names never settle a reading, §14.3).
threads.meaning: A pre-filled confirmation: the values settle the pool (low RSD plus empty covariates), so it takes one accept. The researcher is asked only for the role of levels that are not the pool (process or solvent blank, dilution QC with its factors, LTR or SRM), and which of them were kept out of all fitting so they can serve as the correction's independent check (metab-correction-honest-check). apply_repair reference_rows: exclude.

consumers.inference: Reference rows leave the participant table before the outcome is read, on their own line of the participant flow, and move to the instrument's shelf. Where 'QC' is a level of the outcome itself (another export shape), the task becomes Case vs Control, not three-class.

In exports where 'QC' is a level of the class label, the task is read as three-class and copies of one pooled sample land in the test set, where they are trivially predictable.

threads.title: Pooled QCs drift over injection order within each batch, and batches sit at different levels
threads.detector: Reference rows and feature columns only; a pooled QC is never a participant and never carries the outcome. Per feature, the QC response against injection order with a batch offset: within-batch Spearman statistics summed across batches and tested by permuting order within batch (exact at small n). A per-batch test cannot work at the QC counts exports carry: at 4 QCs per batch the exact two-sided Spearman p is never below 0.083, while the within-batch permutation over two batches of 4 reaches 2/576 = 0.0035. BH across features; a feature counts when |rho| > 0.3 and q < 0.05, and the drifting share is shown beside chance_share at the QC n. Between batches: the shift in QC medians, reported separately so the batch step is never read as drift (pooling all 8 QCs without the offset gives 328/392 features, mostly the step). QC trajectories get a robust LOESS (bisquare) whose span is chosen by leave-one-QC-out CV over interior QCs. Today's engine reading (assay.py:99 drift_reading) correlates order with every numeric column over all 80 rows, participants, age and bmi included; on the fixture that gives 65% drifting, and participants alone give 60%. That study-sample reading is kept, labelled as such, for the no-QC fallback and for metab-run-order-aligned-with-outcome; it is never the drift reading. Alternatives it must reject: a biological trend over order (QCs are one sample, so a trend in them is technical); chance at small n (exact permutation p, FDR, chance share); one bad QC injection (robustness weights); an order column that is really a sample ID or a visit date (the acquisition card).
threads.meaning: Settled on the shared acquisition card, not asked here: the order column is the acquisition sequence (pre-filled, since it is a permutation of row positions), the batch column is the analytical batch, and the QC rows are pooled QCs of this study (metab-reference-rows). The platform comes from the assay card (metab-subdomain).

A feature that drifts below detection late in the run cannot be corrected; it leaves and is listed. The QC filters then run on corrected values, then optional PQN to the QC reference. When sufficiency fails, metab-qc-design-insufficient takes over.

threads.title: Cases and controls (or exposure groups) were run in different parts of the sequence, batches or plates, so drift can impersonate the outcome
threads.detector: Study injections only; a design-balance view of a technical variable, whose require/refuse rule is written before the view is computed. Injection order within batch by outcome level: rank-biserial for a binary outcome, Spearman for continuous, Kruskal-Wallis for multiclass. A Wald-Wolfowitz runs test reads class-block acquisition. Batch and plate x outcome uses Cramer's V (batch.confounding, extended to the injection_order reading; BATCH_KINDS covers batch, run and plate). It is combined with the QC drift reading: drift present and order unbalanced means shortcut risk. Under inference with a declared exposure (diet arm, intake), the same table is read against the exposure. Under prediction, a run-position-only model (order + batch as the only inputs) scored on the same folds gives the shortcut ceiling. The view never reads any feature's relation to the outcome, can only require or refuse corrections, and is recorded as an outcome view. Alternatives it must reject: a randomized order with chance imbalance (effect size and runs test near null); blocked but balanced within blocks (acceptable); an order that follows collection date (asked). On metabolomics_untargeted, order vs responder is AUC 0.545 (near random).
threads.meaning: Asked only when imbalance is detected: was injection order (and plate assignment) randomized with respect to the outcome, and the exposure? The order column's identity comes from the acquisition card.

threads.title: QC RSD fell after correction, but the correction was fitted to make that number small
threads.detector: Leave-one-QC-out corrected RSD over interior QCs only: leaving out the first or last QC of a batch asks the curve to extrapolate, which sufficiency forbids. choose_spans' leave-one-out today includes the end QCs (qc_drift.py:151-163), so its end errors are extrapolation errors. Where present, a second reference never used in fitting (LTR, NIST SRM 1950, or technical duplicates of study samples) gives RSD and replicate correlation before and after correction. The refusal rule carries a margin: with 5 QCs per batch the leave-one-out RSD is noisy, so correction is refused only when the held-out RSD is worse than uncorrected by more than that margin. Alternatives it must reject: overfitting between QCs (an in-sample drop with no held-out drop); over-correction removing biology (the replicate correlation of study duplicates falls).

threads.title: The pooled QC does not contain what the study samples contain
threads.detector: Per feature, detection rate in QCs vs in study samples. Flags features detected in at least 50% of study samples but in under 70% of QCs (the QC detection filter would delete them), and features whose QC median falls outside the study 5-95% range; a PCA projection checks that the QCs sit near the study centroid. It reads participants' feature values, never the outcome; used as a filter rule under prediction, the study-sample half runs in training folds. Pooling dilutes any feature present in only a minority of participants, so even a pool of all samples can fail the 70% rule for them; the decision is keyed on the measured mismatch, not on how the pool was made. Other sources of mismatch: a subset pool (e.g. controls only), a commercial surrogate QC (matrix mismatch), a diluted pool.

threads.title: Each feature's technical noise in the QCs, relative to its spread across people, is a reliability, not just a filter
threads.detector: After drift correction, per feature on the log scale, on detected and never imputed values: QC detection rate (at least 70%), QC RSD (below 20% for LC, 30% for GC), and the D-ratio, SD across QCs over SD across study samples (below 50%), with the study SD from training rows only (DRatioFilter). Technical reliability is lambda_tech = 1 - D^2. Because the filter keeps only D < 0.5, every kept feature has lambda_tech above 0.75 (measured minimum on the fixture 0.750), so the correction can move a kept effect by at most a third. With covariates Z, the relevant reliability is the conditional one, 1 - sigma2_tech / Var(X | Z), which is smaller than 1 - D^2; for logistic models the correction is approximate. SD_QC is measured at the pool's level, so it understates the error for participants near the floor. On metabolomics_untargeted raw values, 41% of features have QC RSD above 30% before correction, and 54 are detected in fewer than 70% of QCs. Alternatives it must reject: a D shrunk by imputed ties (un-imputed values are used); saturated QCs (metab-dilution-linearity); QCs injected back to back that understate variance (the spacing check).

threads.detector: Blank rows come from the sample-role census. The detector also reads a numeric limit attached to the token, a kit limit table (LOD/LLOQ/ULOQ per analyte), or a pile-up at one value (a limit the exporter substituted, such as LOD/2 written in). Alternatives it must reject: a token meaning 'not measured' or 'sample failed' (QNS, hemolyzed), which is missing, not censored (§14.2); a pile-up that is a genuinely common value.
threads.meaning: Stated from the grammar. Asked only for unknown tokens or missing limit values: what each token means (below detection, below quantification, above the upper limit, not measured) and the limit value when it is not written.

consumers.inference: Each flagged cell becomes a censored value with its side and limit, not a blank. A column is never dropped for its text.
Left-censored at the LOD (Tobit MI, metab-left-censored-nondetects). Values between LOD and LLOQ are kept as detected but imprecise. Right-censored at the ULOQ, never median-filled.
consumers.prediction: In-fold and outcome-blind: left at the stated limit (LogScaleCensoredFill with the given LOD), right at the ULOQ. Exporter-substituted constants are recognized as limits.

consumers.inference: A plateau at the ULOQ is not offered as a threshold shape (metab-dilution-linearity).

threads.title: The batches were already corrected before export, possibly with the outcome in the model
threads.detector: Outcome-blind signatures, read when a batch or plate column is present: (1) within-batch variances equalized per feature across batches (ComBat's scale step); (2) a study-sample between-batch shift far below the shift the QCs still show (the QCs were left out of the correction); (3) both shifts at zero to numerical precision (mean or median centring). Exporter metadata that names a correction (MetaboAnalyst, sva) settles it. Equal batch medians alone detect centring, not ComBat (empirical-Bayes shrinkage leaves small residual differences), and outcome-protected ComBat in an unbalanced design leaves study-sample batch means apart in proportion to the outcome imbalance, so medians alone would miss the dangerous case. Contrast with the drift reading: within-batch drift may remain while between-batch steps vanish. Alternatives it must reject: a well-behaved instrument (QC medians differ by noise, and within-batch variances are not equalized); a batch column that is not the analytical batch (the acquisition card).
threads.meaning: The researcher says whether a between-batch correction was applied before export, which method, and whether the outcome or exposure was a covariate in it.

consumers.inference: No second correction; batch is kept as a covariate. If the outcome was protected in an unbalanced design, the app states that group differences may be inflated and asks for the uncorrected export.
consumers.prediction: A correction fitted on all rows before the split has seen the test rows (and the labels, if protected). The honest path is the uncorrected export with ReferenceComBat fitted in-fold.

consumers.inference: Featurewise results from outcome-protected, pre-corrected, unbalanced data are not reported as confirmatory.
n/a
consumers.prediction: The score is labelled optimistic when the correction saw the test rows.

consumers.inference: Method and covariates of the prior correction stated, with its consequence.

threads.failure_prevented: ComBat with the group as a covariate in an unbalanced design manufactures FDR-significant differences (Nygaard 2016). In prediction, a correction that saw the test rows inflates the score, and the uploaded file looks clean.
threads.magic: 'Within each batch, every feature's spread is the same to three decimals, and your study samples' batch shift is a tenth of the shift your QCs still show: someone batch-corrected this file and left the QCs out. If the case label was in that correction, and cases were 70% of batch 1, part of any difference you find was put there by it.'
threads.layout: Angles: 'Were the batches already aligned?' (per-feature within-batch SDs and study-sample batch shifts beside the QC shifts) | 'Was the outcome in the correction?' (batch x outcome table, a design view).
threads.sentence: Data were supplied after {method} batch correction {with | without} {outcome} as a covariate; {consequence}.

threads.title: Is the metabolome the exposure, the outcome of a diet, or the path between them?
threads.detector: The roles reading: an exposure column that is not a feature (intervention arm, intake, a diet score) beside the metabolite block and an outcome. The detector also states the featurewise direction the engine would take today: a numeric outcome gives outcome ~ x_j + Z; a two-level outcome gives x_j ~ event + Z (featurewise.py:14-17), so a continuous exposure with the metabolome as the outcome block is not reachable. No value test can settle a causal role, so it is user-settled (§14.3), with the guess pre-filled from the declared roles.
threads.meaning: On the study-question card (with sample timing and matched design): metabolites as exposures of an outcome; metabolites as outcomes of an exposure ('which metabolites does the diet change?'); metabolites as mediators (meet-in-the-middle); or metabolites as markers of intake.

consumers.inference: For diet -> metabolite: adjust for confounders of both (age, sex, kidney function, fasting; BMI only if not a mediator). For the total effect of diet on disease, metabolites are never adjusted for (overadjustment). For mediation, mediator-outcome confounders are required.
consumers.prediction: The metabolome is the input block. 'Predict intake from the metabolome' (a biomarker panel) is a different outcome, and is asked.

consumers.inference: Metabolome as outcome block: metabolite_j ~ exposure + Z, one model per metabolite with BH (the limma design), so the metabolite's technical error sits in the response (precision, not bias). When the exposure is self-reported intake, its own error attenuates this slope, so the dietary lens's calibration thread applies. Metabolome as exposure: outcome ~ metabolite_j + Z, where metabolite error attenuates (metab-feature-technical-reliability).
consumers.prediction: Fixed by what is to be predicted.

consumers.inference: Worded by direction: 'per weekly serving, metabolite X rose 12%' vs 'per doubling of X, the odds of T2D'. Mediation proportions only with the meet-in-the-middle criteria met.
consumers.prediction: Importance is read as association, never as mechanism.

consumers.inference: Role, direction, adjustment set and any intake calibration stated.

threads.failure_prevented: A score-driven pipeline always places the metabolome on the predictor side. Diet's effect on metabolites is then estimated in reverse, and adjusting for metabolites blocks the diet effect it meant to estimate. Self-reported intake error, ignored, attenuates every metabolite-on-diet slope.
threads.magic: 'You have a fish-intake column and 392 metabolites. Asked "which metabolites does fish raise?", each metabolite is the outcome. The default direction would have regressed fish intake on each metabolite: an answer to a question you did not ask. And because fish intake is self-reported, its own error shrinks every slope; the dietary calibration applies here too.'
threads.layout: Routing: the lineage showing the metabolite block moving between the exposure side and the outcome side, with the adjustment set redrawn.
threads.sentence: Each metabolite was modeled as an outcome of {exposure} (one linear model per metabolite on log2 values, adjusted for {Z}; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR){; intake was corrected for measurement error by regression calibration}.
sources: Schisterman EF, Cole SR, Platt RW 2009, Epidemiology 20:488-495
VanderWeele TJ 2015, Explanation in Causal Inference (Oxford University Press)
Smyth GK 2004, Stat Appl Genet Mol Biol 3:Article 3
Carroll RJ et al. 2006, Measurement Error in Nonlinear Models, 2nd ed.

threads.title: The outcome is defined by a metabolite that is in the panel (glucose for diabetes, creatinine for CKD, urate for gout)
threads.detector: Outcome-blind first: the outcome's definition (asked, or from the codebook) is matched against annotated features with a dictionary of defining analytes (diabetes: glucose; CKD: creatinine, cystatin C; gout: urate; dyslipidemia: triglycerides and cholesterol esters in lipidomics), extending covariate_guesses' outcome-group map to features. Prediction only, inside training folds: a single feature whose relation to the outcome is a step near a clinical cutoff (single-feature AUC >= 0.95) is proposed for meaning review, recorded. The MS feature measures the defining analyte with different error from the clinical assay, so separation is near-deterministic rather than exact. Whether this is leakage depends on timing (metab-sample-timing-vs-diagnosis): in a prevalent or same-visit design it is the definition; in an incident design, baseline glucose is the legitimate clinical baseline to beat. Alternatives: a strong genuine biomarker that is not definitional (asked); an annotation mismatch (metab-annotation-confidence).
threads.meaning: The researcher confirms the outcome's definition, that feature X is or measures the defining analyte, and (from the timing card) whether the design is prevalent or incident.

consumers.decision: route out, redefine, or treat as baseline
consumers.inference: Prevalent or same-visit design: the defining analyte and its adduct group are routed out, or the outcome is redefined. Adjusting for it is not offered, because with a deterministic threshold the model is not estimable (separation). Incident design: the analyte stays out of the metabolite block and becomes part of the clinical comparator (metab-clinical-factors).
consumers.prediction: Prevalent: routed out of the inputs by rule, scores with and without recorded. Incident: baseline glucose joins the clinical-only baseline the metabolites must beat.

consumers.inference: n/a
consumers.prediction: The headline score excludes the defining analyte (prevalent) or is the increment over it (incident), paired fold by fold.

consumers.inference: Named as the outcome's definition, not a discovery.
Stated.

threads.failure_prevented: The model 'discovers' that glucose predicts diabetes defined by glucose. The AUC is the definition, and the reported panel's novelty is zero. Or, in a prospective design, baseline glucose is wrongly thrown away when it is the bar the metabolites must clear.

threads.title: Some samples were drawn after diagnosis or treatment began: the metabolome may be the disease, not its risk
threads.detector: Sample collection date against diagnosis or event date gives each case's lag. Dates are parsed by their values (repeats.py:112), or a prevalent/incident flag is read. The view shows the lag distribution among cases: the share drawn after diagnosis, and the share within 2 years before. It reads when the outcome happened (the outcome alone plus a design column), never the outcome's relation to features, so it is allowed before the lock. Alternatives: a date that is the processing or analysis date (asked); controls' dates, which are the index date of their matched case (metab-matched-sets).
threads.meaning: On the study-question card: whether samples precede diagnosis (a prospective nested design) or follow it (prevalent cases, possibly treated), and what each date means. Becomes stated when collection and diagnosis dates give the lag strip.

consumers.inference: Cases sampled after diagnosis are excluded or analyzed separately. A lag exclusion (first 1-2 years) is a pre-specified sensitivity analysis.
consumers.prediction: The intended use (screening years ahead vs at presentation) fixes which samples are eligible.

consumers.inference: A post-diagnosis sample estimates a disease signature (consequence), not a risk association, and the estimand is stated. The answer also decides metab-outcome-defined-by-a-feature (prevalent vs incident).
After the lock, estimates by lag stratum.
consumers.prediction: Score by time-to-diagnosis stratum. A model trained on samples drawn at diagnosis is not scored as a years-ahead predictor.

consumers.inference: After the lock, features whose association is concentrated in short-lag cases are flagged as plausibly early disease.

Which question are you answering: risk, or signature?' After the lock, the by-lag comparison shows whether the signal holds in samples drawn five or more years ahead.

threads.title: The rows are matched case-control sets, not independent people
threads.detector: A set-identifier column whose sets each contain exactly one case (or a fixed case:control ratio). Members agree on candidate matching factors: age within a few years, sex, fasting status, storage time, batch. The outcome is balanced exactly by design (outcome alone). grain.py recognizes the shape only through DESIGN_NOT_DESCRIBED. Alternatives: repeat samples of one person (metab-person-fingerprint); households or sites (asked); a frequency-matched design without sets.
threads.meaning: On the study-question card: the matched sets, the matching factors, and the case:control ratio.

consumers.inference: The matched set is the unit, and every split keeps a set together.
Matching factors are not estimated (their effects are fixed by design). Residual confounding by them is stated.
consumers.prediction: Matching factors cannot show added value inside the matched sample (Janes & Pepe 2008).

consumers.inference: Conditional logistic regression for each feature. An unconditional model is disclosed as biased under fine matching.
consumers.prediction: The case fraction is fixed by design, so predicted probabilities are not risks.

consumers.inference: Set-grouped resampling for intervals.
consumers.prediction: Folds by set. AUC within a sample matched on predictors misstates population discrimination. Calibration is reweighted to cohort incidence, or not reported.

consumers.inference: Matched design and conditional analysis stated.

threads.failure_prevented: An unconditional analysis of a finely matched design biases odds ratios. Random folds split sets, so the model learns set-level patterns (plate, storage) shared by a case and its control. Probabilities from a 1:1 matched design are read as risks.

threads.title: Repeated samples from one person are more alike than any intervention effect: the metabolome is a fingerprint
threads.detector: Subject IDs repeat (_repeated_subjects routes to set_grain). As a value test on predictors only: within-person vs between-person profile correlation, the per-feature share of variance between people, and a nearest-profile identification rate (how often a sample's closest other sample belongs to the same person) against chance. Alternatives: technical replicates (closer still, same date; metab-technical-replicates); unrelated people under one ID (identification rate at chance). metabolomics_paired_logged carries IDs with no biological pairing, so it is a working negative control.
threads.meaning: Settled on the shared repeat-grain question: the repeats are the same person at different times (pre/post, crossover period, repeat visit). Under prediction, whether the model is for a new person or a known person over time is asked on the deployment question.

With random folds the model scored 0.95 by recognizing people; grouped by person, it is 0.64. Paired, each change is measured against the person's own baseline, not the crowd.' threads.title: The next batch, lab or platform will not look like these: the honest score is across batches
threads.detector: After correction, the residual between-batch shift, all outcome-blind: QC medians per batch, study-sample RLA medians, and the share of top-PC variance explained by batch. Also the number of batches, sites, instruments or platforms, and whether feature IDs are lab-specific (m/z@RT). Under prediction, the leave-one-batch-out score beside the random-fold score, and calibration-in-the-large per held-out batch. With 2 batches LOBO is only 2 folds, so its spread is shown. Alternatives: a residual shift within QC noise (no transport problem); batch confounded with the outcome (metab-run-order-aligned-with-outcome takes precedence).

threads.title: With 392 features and 72 people, noise alone reaches a high score: the bar any finding must clear
threads.detector: Outcome-blind: the shape (n, events, p, and the effective number of quantities from metab-one-compound-many-features). Random labels are drawn with the outcome's own class counts (its marginal only, never its pairing with features) against the actual feature matrix, giving the null distribution of the best single-feature association (max |t| or AUC) and of the full pipeline's cross-validated score. Then, as recorded outcome views: under prediction, the honest score's label-permutation p-value with every filter, screen and tuning step inside the permutation (Ojala & Garriga 2010); under inference, after the lock, the metabolome-wide significance level by permutation. Whole-pipeline permutation is CPU-heavy: it is scheduled, or run with fewer permutations and a Monte Carlo interval on its p. Alternative: a ceiling inflated by one outlier sample (rank statistics).

Under inference: for any multivariable selection, the bootstrap inclusion frequency (Heinze 2018). The outcome-blind precursor is p/n and redundancy, which predict instability before any fit. Alternative: instability within a compound group only, where the group itself is stable (metab-one-compound-many-features).

threads.title: Two features are a substrate and its product: their ratio indexes a pathway step, and it cancels dilution
threads.detector: Outcome-blind: annotated substrate-product or precursor-product pairs from a pathway table among features at MSI level 2 or better (kynurenine/tryptophan, citrulline/ornithine/arginine, the BCAA/AAA Fischer ratio, lysoPC/PC, ADMA/arginine). For each pair: whether the ratio is more reliable than its parts (QC RSD of the ratio below both) and whether it is dilution-invariant (uncorrelated with the PQN dilution factor while the parts are not; a common dilution cancels in a log difference). A ratio is never chosen by its association with the outcome before the lock. Under prediction, an all-pairs ratio search is a proposal that runs inside folds and is recorded. Alternative: pairs that only co-vary through dilution, whose ratio carries nothing new.

threads.title: The assay block is affinity proteomics (Olink NPX or SomaScan RFU), with vendor normalization, plates and LOD flags
threads.detector: Outcome-blind. Olink naming (OID, UniProt, NPX) or SomaScan naming (seq.NNNN.NN, RFU). NPX values are on a log2 relative scale, can be negative, and plate medians sit near zero after normalization; RFU values are positive and log-normal. Signs of vendor processing: per-sample QC or assay warning columns, per-assay LOD columns, a plate ID, and bridging samples (one sample ID on two plates). It must reject MS intensities and expression matrices.

journey_load:
TYPICAL STUDY (untargeted LC-MS plasma, binary outcome, like metabolomics_untargeted). Tier counts across the 42 threads: 11 asked (most of them conditional), 8 surfaced, 16 stated, 6 silent, 1 parked.

Questions are grouped into shared cards, so no fact is asked twice:
1. Assay card (metab-subdomain), always asked once and pre-filled: platform, LC vs GC, matrix, any measured normalizer, and prior processing (only when the range signal fires alone).
2. Reference rows and acquisition card, pre-filled; usually one accept:
   - pool and roles from values (metab-reference-rows);
   - order and batch columns (metab-qc-drift);
   - 'was the run randomized?' only when imbalance fires;
   - 'were QCs run but not exported?' only when no_pooled_qc fires.
3. Study-question card: metabolome role, sample timing, matched sets. Asked only when an exposure column, a disease-state outcome or a set ID exists.
4. Cross-lens covariate-role card (metab-clinical-factors). Not a new metabolomics question.
5. Repeat-grain question, shared by technical-replicates, person-fingerprint and low-biological-ICC. Only when IDs or profiles repeat.
6. Deployment question, under prediction only: new batch, lab or re-assay; new vs known person; short panel vs best score.

Fixed asks: 2 to 4 cards (3 to 5 under prediction). Conditional asks, each firing in about one journey in three or fewer: treatment marker, defining analyte, pre-corrected batches, urine normalizer, pre-analytical protocol.

Surfaced noticings: 5 to 7 per journey:
- QC drift strip with run-order balance
- non-detect mechanism
- missing-by-batch, when present
- features vs compounds
- noise ceiling
- person fingerprint, when repeats exist
Under prediction, panel stability is added. The feature-flow screen is the single place where every filter threshold is fixed. It absorbs five threads' threshold decisions.

On metabolomics_untargeted itself the journey is light:
- Asked: the assay card and the covariate-role card (plus deployment under prediction).
- Stated: reference rows (one accept), QC insufficiency with the fallback pre-selected (4 QCs per batch, 18 unbracketed injections), PQN as default (a negative control at AUC 0.535), and the feature flow.
- Surfaced: the drift strip (run-order balance at 0.545 becomes one methods line), the -0.99 non-detect figure, and the noise ceiling (mz_0094 at the null).

Load controls still owed:
- Explanation: a top feature could carry about 10 badges (drift rho, D-ratio, censoring, blank ratio, MSI level, selection frequency, treatment or definitional flag). Show one trust row per feature with only the failing badges.
- Evaluation under prediction: up to about 11 alternate scores (correction off, raw vs PQN, two fills, run-position baseline, clinical baseline, LOBO, grouped vs random folds, with/without flagged rows, permutation null). Show one ladder with only the deltas above a stated margin.
- Compute: whole-pipeline label permutation multiplied by these refits is a long CPU-heavy run on the machine beside the bed. Schedule it with Nolan, or run fewer permutations with a Monte Carlo interval.
report:
The final metabolomics catalog has 42 threads after the critic's verdicts: 0 cut, 2 moved to silent, every fix applied, and tiers and rank signals taken from the overwhelm critic. The 24 fixed threads each name their change in critic_notes.

WHAT WAS CHANGED
- **Nothing cut.** The critic marked metab-enrichment-background 'cut', but the evidence check found it sound. The rule cuts only when both reject, so it stays, parked at the lowest tier as a requirement for any future pathway feature. If you would rather cut whatever the skeptic alone rejects, this is the only thread affected.
- **Moved to silent:** metab-variance-structure and metab-detectable-effect (the two automate-silently verdicts).
- **Tiers:**
  - asked: 11, mostly conditional
  - surfaced: 8
  - stated: 16
  - silent: 6
  - parked: 1
- **Fixes that change engine work, not just wording:**
  1. **qc-drift:** the detector is now QC-only, with a batch offset and an exact or permutation p. assay.py:99 drift_reading tests all 80 rows, including age and bmi, and stays only as the study-sample reading for the no-QC fallback and the run-order thread. At 4 QCs per batch, a per-batch Spearman test can never reach significance (p ≥ 0.083). Permuting within batch across both batches can (minimum p = 2/576). The AUC 0.31 → 0.49 figures came from the fixtures finder's linear detrend, not an engine path, so they are dropped.
  2. **qc-design-insufficient:** the fixture has 4 QCs per batch and 9 unbracketed study injections at the end of each batch, 18 in all. sufficiency (qc_drift.py:220) returns at the QC count before it checks bracketing, so reporting both reasons is new work.
  3. **correction-honest-check:** choose_spans' leave-one-out (qc_drift.py:151-163) includes the end QCs, where the curve has to extrapolate. The held-out RSD now uses interior QCs only, and refusing a correction needs a margin.
  4. **feature-technical-reliability:** the D < 0.5 filter already guarantees lambda > 0.75, so the prediction flag moves to lambda < 0.9. Reliability is conditional on the covariates, and the magic's arithmetic is corrected.
  5. **pre-corrected-batches:** the detector now uses outcome-blind signatures: equalized within-batch variances, and a study-sample batch shift far below the QC shift. These catch ComBat and outcome-protected corrections; equal batch medians only catch simple centring.
  6. **outcome-defined-by-a-feature:** split into prevalent vs incident designs, gated by sample timing. 'Adjust for glucose' is removed, because the model cannot be estimated when the outcome is a glucose threshold.
  7. **metabolome-role:** self-reported intake error is wired to the dietary lens's calibration thread.
  8. **Smaller fixes:**
     - reference-rows magic matches the fixture: QC is a level of sample_type, responder is NaN on QC rows, and 'less than half' replaces 'a quarter'.
     - zeros: the '14 log units' claim is corrected (zeros sit about 3.9 ln units below the minimum of 50.95), and a test of zero share against abundance is added.
     - S080 on merged_modes anchors failed-injection.
     - IS magic is re-anchored, since the D-ratio filter already removes standards.
     - Dilution-linearity uses a single threshold, r < 0.7.
     - ICC magic says 'nearly triples'.
     - glog effects are reported on log2.
     - Each compound's representative is chosen without looking at the outcome.
     - Split features merge only on an m/z and RT match.
     - The normalizer comparison runs only after the lock.
     - The pre-analytical outcome table is disclosure only.
     - clinical-factors uses a fold-paired AUC or log-likelihood difference, or a decision curve, instead of NRI or DeLong.
     - The noise ceiling uses the real 39/33 split.
     - Ratios are worded as pathway-step indices.
- **Shared cards replace duplicated questions:**
  - assay: platform, matrix, prior processing
  - acquisition and reference roles
  - study question: role, timing, matched sets
  - repeat grain
  - deployment, under prediction only
  - cross-lens covariate roles

WHAT IS MEASURED VS ILLUSTRATIVE
- **Measured or checked on fixtures:**
  - QC RSD 0.25 vs 0.59
  - non-detect rho −0.99; 304 of 392 features have blanks
  - QC positions, and 18 unbracketed injections
  - order vs responder AUC 0.545
  - total signal vs responder AUC 0.535
  - 22 features with |rho| > 0.3 against BMI
  - minimum lambda 0.750
  - noise ceiling ~0.69 (analytic) vs mz_0094 at 0.702
  - merged_modes counts and S080
  - zeros range 50.95 to 4.54e6
  - 404 features in about 100 compounds
- **Illustrative, describing a case the thread would catch:** metformin, glucose, urine dilution, matched pairs, the 88% fingerprint, the LOBO scores, the 38 spared features, the 188-analyte kit panel, storage time.

For this pass I only read fixture notes and code. I ran nothing; the measured numbers come from the critic's run and the fixture notes. Two citations rest on memory because web checks were blocked: the NRI critique (Kerr 2014; Pepe 2013) and Badawy & Guillemin 2019 on the kynurenine/tryptophan ratio. The metformin example still needs a metabolomics-specific source.

GAPS NOT YET THREADED (Nolan's completeness concern; for the next round, unreviewed)
- Medications that confound but do not treat the outcome, such as statins in a diet study. These are found only through metadata.
- Ion suppression and matrix effects.
- Retention-time misalignment beyond splits across batches.
- A fasting-state signature in the features (ketone bodies) when there is no fasting column.
- The food-xenobiotic intake bridge, which treatment-marker refers to but which has no thread of its own.

COMPUTE: whole-pipeline label permutation times the sensitivity refits is a long CPU-heavy run on the machine beside Nolan's bed. Schedule it with him, or run fewer permutations with a Monte Carlo interval.
